phase2_recipe:
Run the source repository's TabR evaluation on Covertype exactly as `python bin/tabr.py exp/tabr/covtype/2-lr-evaluation/0.toml --force` runs it, with every setting taken from that config and the remaining defaults of `Model` in `bin/tabr.py`, the training seed (`delu.random.seed(C.seed)`) supplied by `--seed` in place of the config's top-level `seed`. Obtain the data the way the README's Data section does: download `data.tar` from `https://huggingface.co/datasets/puhsu/tabular-benchmarks/resolve/main/data.tar` and extract `data/covtype/`, whose fixed split (`X_num_*.npy`, 10 float32 numeric columns; `X_bin_*.npy`, 44 float32 0/1 columns; `Y_*.npy`, int64 labels 0 to 6; `info.json` with `task_type` multiclass) has 371,847 train, 92,962 val and 116,203 test rows; do not re-split or reshuffle it, and the test split contains all 7 classes. Preprocess as `lib.build_dataset` does for the config's `num_policy = "quantile"` with `[data] seed = 0` (`transform_num` in `lib/data.py`): fit `sklearn.preprocessing.QuantileTransformer(output_distribution="normal", n_quantiles=max(min(N // 30, 1000), 10), subsample=1_000_000_000, random_state=0)` on the training numeric columns after adding per-column Gaussian noise of scale `1e-3 / max(std, 1e-3)` from `np.random.default_rng(0)`, then transform the un-noised train, val and test numeric columns; the 44 binary columns pass through untouched, there are no categorical columns, and `cat_policy` and `y_policy` are null. Build the `Model` of `bin/tabr.py` at the config: `LREmbeddings` with `d_embedding` 36 on the 10 numeric features, `d_main` 130, `d_multiplier` 2.0, `encoder_n_blocks` 1, `predictor_n_blocks` 1, `mixer_normalization` auto, `context_dropout` 0.0437357558538884, `dropout0` 0.5343904237887059, `dropout1` 0.0, LayerNorm, ReLU, and a 7-way output head (`lib.get_d_out(7)`), 276,847 parameters in total. Retrieval is the source's exact squared-L2 nearest-neighbour search with `context_size` 96 over the training split: during training the current batch is removed from the candidates in `apply_model`, concatenated back at the front of the candidate keys inside `forward`, searched with k = 97, and each row's own index is removed so that 96 neighbours remain; when val or test rows are scored all 371,847 training rows are candidates and k = 96, and candidate keys are re-encoded on every forward pass (`memory_efficient` is False by default). Train with `F.cross_entropy` on the 7-way logits, batch size 1024 drawn from a fresh random permutation of the training rows every epoch (364 batches, the last one partial), AdamW at learning rate 0.0004585278054026558 with weight decay 0.0 and PyTorch's default betas and epsilon, no learning-rate schedule and no gradient clipping, `n_epochs = inf`. After every epoch score the val and test splits in eval mode with all dropout off, every row once in order (the source's `evaluate`, `eval_batch_size` 32768), computing accuracy as `lib.metrics.calculate_metrics` does for `prediction_type = "logits"` on a NumPy copy of the logits: softmax over the 7 classes, argmax, then `sklearn.metrics.classification_report(y_true, labels, output_dict=True)["accuracy"]`, i.e. plain top-1 accuracy over all 7 classes as a fraction on the 0 to 1 scale, which is the `score` for this multiclass task; the log-loss the source also records is not needed. Early stopping is delu's `ProgressTracker(patience=16)` on the validation score: a strictly higher validation accuracy makes a new best epoch whose parameters are checkpointed, and training stops once more than 16 consecutive epochs pass without one. At the end reload the best-epoch checkpoint and re-score train, val and test with the same procedure, as `bin/tabr.py` does before writing `report.json` (train rows are still excluded from their own candidates there, as `apply_model` does for `part == "train"`). The number to write is that reloaded single model's test accuracy, with no ensembling, together with its val and train accuracies, the best epoch and the number of epochs run.
Write the metrics JSON with at least: {"test_accuracy": float, "val_accuracy": float, "train_accuracy": float, "best_epoch": int, "epochs_run": int, "n_parameters": int, "wall_seconds": float, "device_count": int}
